blocks.text: Big O notation algorithm ki time complexity bayan karne ka mathematical (math wala) tareeqa hai. Yeh batata hai ke input size barhne par algorithm ko mukammal hone mein zyada se zyada kitna waqt lagega (upper bound, oopri had). Is notation se alag alag algorithms ki efficiency ka comparison aasan ho jata hai, kyun ke un ki performance ki saaf tasveer milti hai.
Big O Notation kaise kaam karta hai
Big O notation symbols ke zariye batata hai ke input ka size badalne par algorithm ka runtime kaise badalta hai. Kuch aam misalein:

items: O(1) Constant Time: runtime input ke size ke saath nahi badalta. Maslan array mein kisi khaas item ko us ke index se parhna constant time hai, kyun ke array chhota ho ya bara, waqt utna hi lagta hai.

O(n) Linear Time: runtime input ke size ke saath seedha (linearly) barhta hai. Misal: college mein n students hain, har ek ki alag student ID hai. Kisi khaas student ko tamam n students ki list mein dhoondna ho to waqt is par depend karta hai ke kitne students check karne parte hain. Worst case (sab se buri soorat) mein jo student hum dhoond rahe hain woh list mein bilkul aakhri ho sakta hai, yani tamam n students check karne honge. Har student ko ek ek kar ke dekhna parta hai, is liye waqt n ke proportional (saath saath barhne wala) hai. Is liye yeh linear time complexity O(n) hai: students barhne ke saath waqt seedha barhta hai.

O(n²) Quadratic Time: input barhne par runtime quadratically (n ke square, yani n x n, ki tarah) barhta hai. Misal: college ke n students programming competition mein hain aur behtareen team chunne ke liye har do students (har pair) ki performance ko compare karna hai. Is ke liye har student ko baqi har student se compare karna hoga. Zaroori comparisons ki ginti pehle n − 1 integers ka sum (jor) hai: 1 + 2 + … + (n − 1) = n(n − 1)/2. Is liye is kaam ki time complexity quadratic, O(n²), hai: students barhne par waqt n² ki tarah barhta hai.

O(log n) Logarithmic Time: runtime logarithmically barhta hai, yani input ke muqable mein bohat aahista. Misal: college ke n students ke saath andaza lagane (guessing) ka khel. Ek student 1 se n ke darmiyan koi number sochta hai aur aap ko woh number boojhna hai. Har andaze ke baad student batata hai ke asal number aap ke andaze se bara hai ya chhota. Range ke beech se shuru kar ke aur jawab ke mutabiq andaza badal kar aap mumkin numbers jaldi kam kar lete hain. Sahi number tak pohanchne ke andazon ki ginti is ke proportional hai ke range kitni dafa aadhi ho sakti hai, jo logarithmic hai. Is liye is khel ki time complexity O(log n) hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne heading mein “O(n2)” chhapa hai; matlab O(n²) yani n ka square hai. Kitab comparisons ki ginti “n(n − 1)” likhti hai, magar pehle n − 1 integers ka sum theek n(n − 1)/2 hai, kyun ke har jora sirf ek dafa compare hota hai. Maslan 4 students: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 = 4 x 3 / 2. Time complexity phir bhi O(n²) hi hai.

blocks.alt: Big O Notation title wala graph: vertical axis (khari line) par Time aur horizontal axis (leti line) par Input Size. O(1) seedhi barabar lakeer; O(log n) pehle tezi se uthti phir taqreeban barabar ho jati hai; O(n) seedhi uthti lakeer; O(n²) tezi se oopar murti hai.

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Kitab mein is graph ke neeche ghalti se 'Figure 1.1: System development life cycle stages' chhapa hai; yeh asal mein Big O Notation ka graph hai. Input Size barhne par dekhein: O(1) ki lakeer barabar rehti hai (waqt nahi badalta), O(log n) bohat aahista barhti hai, O(n) seedhi barhti hai aur O(n²) sab se tez oopar jati hai. Is liye bare input par O(1) < O(log n) < O(n) < O(n²).

Alag alag time complexities ka comparison karte waqt yeh samajhna zaroori hai ke input n ka size barhne par algorithm ka zaroori waqt kaise barhta hai. Constant time O(1) n ke size se nahi badalta: input jitna bhi bara ho, waqt utna hi lagta hai; graph mein yeh seedhi barabar (flat) lakeer hai.
Yeh program input size n ke liye har complexity ke taqreeban qadam (steps) print karta hai. n ki value 16 se 32, 1000 waghaira kar ke Run karein aur dekhein kaun tezi se barhta hai.

n = 16   # input size

def halving_steps(size):
    steps = 0
    while size > 1:
        size = size // 2      # cut the work in half each time
        steps += 1
    return steps

print("Input size n =", n)
print("O(1)     :", 1, "step")
print("O(log n) :", halving_steps(n), "steps")
print("O(n)     :", n, "steps")
print("O(n^2)   :", n * n, "steps")

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"n = 16": input size.
"def halving_steps(size):": ginta hai ke size ko baar baar aadha karte karte 1 tak pohanchne mein kitne qadam lagte hain; yahi O(log n) hai.
"size = size // 2" aur "steps += 1": har chakkar mein kaam aadha aur ginti ek barhti hai.
"print(\"O(1)     :\", 1, ...)": constant (hamesha ek jaisa) kaam: 1 step.
"print(\"O(n)     :\", n, ...)" aur "n * n": linear mein n steps, quadratic mein n x n steps.
Output: "Input size n = 16", phir O(1) = 1 step, O(log n) = 4 steps (16, 8, 4, 2, 1), O(n) = 16 steps, O(n^2) = 256 steps.
Khud try karein: n = 32 kar ke Run karein: O(log n) sirf 5 ho jata hai jabke O(n^2) 1024 ho jata hai.

blocks.prompt: 1,000 students ke liye andaze ke khel mein taqreeban kitne andaze, aur har pair ke comparisons wale O(n²) kaam mein kitne comparisons chahiyein?
blocks.explanation: Taqreeban 10 andaze, kyun ke 2¹⁰ = 1024 (range har dafa aadhi hoti hai). Aur 1000 x 999 / 2 = 499,500 comparisons.

items: Big O: input barhne par waqt ki oopri had.
Bare n par: O(1) < O(log n) < O(n) < O(n²).
